title: Question about using the proper model for a turn based game.
author: wwlima
selftext:
Hi everyone,

My favorite hobby lately has been making my own games. After releasing a night-time city driving game (it's complete, though I still add a few features here and there), I'm now working on a turn-based RPG with hex-grid combat.

I'm not worrying about graphics right now, just the game's core structure. Do you think Sonnet 5.5 or Sol 6.2 on high effort is enough to fix bugs and add new gameplay elements—like skills, dialogue, and new quests (nothing that hasn't already been done in other released games)—or do you think it's better to have everything guided by Opus or Astra? (I'm paying for the Plus plans on both ChatGPT and Claude.)

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
If you gave the right skills you can do it with Sonnet.

Sol is more powerful, you can make a game with Sol, too.

comments.author: ChadSexman
comments.body:
Personally I use both.

Claude for architecture and code, Codex for anything requiring spatial relationships or textures.

For your specific use case, I’d use Opus 5.5 for implementation and Fable for planning.
